svg.aria-label: A basketball half court, seen from above
svg.title: NBA half court, plan view, drawn to the real dimensions
svg.desc:
ONE unit = 0.1 ft. The viewBox is the half court itself: 500 x 470 = 50 ft wide by 47 ft deep, with 7 units of bleed on every side so the boundary strokes are not clipped in half. Every number below is a real measurement, not an eyeball.
court width 50 ft x 0 .. 500 half court depth 47 ft y 0 (baseline) .. 470 (half court line) basket centre 5 ft 3 in (250, 52.5) rim 18 in diameter r 7.5 backboard 6 ft, 4 ft out y 40, x 220 .. 280 restricted area 4 ft radius r 40 from the basket centre the key 16 ft wide x 170 .. 330 free throw line 19 ft y 190 free throw circle 12 ft diameter r 60, centred ON the free throw line three point arc 23 ft 9 in r 237.5 from the basket centre corner three 3 ft from the sideline, x 30 and x 470 arc / corner join y 141.98 = 52.5 + sqrt(237.5^2 - 220^2), i.e. the exact tangent point, which is why the published "14 ft" is really 14.2 top of the arc 29 ft from the baseline = 61.7% of the half court depth centre circle 12 ft diameter r 60 at (250, 470), top half visible block 7 ft from the baseline, on both lane lines
THE ONE DELIBERATE UNTRUTH: real court lines are 2 in wide (1.67 units). At the size this is ever rendered that is a hairline, so the strokes are 2.5 (3 in). Nothing else here is approximated.
The corner threes are STRAIGHT LINES and that is the whole point of drawing this properly. An arc that runs sideline to sideline is the single most common way a hand drawn court gives itself away, and this project has already shipped one corner three bug.
